The trilogy was a great financial success, with the films collectively being among the highest-grossing film series of all time. The films were critically acclaimed and heavily awarded, winning 17 out of 30 Academy Awards nominated in total. The final film in the trilogy, The Return of the King, won all 11 of the Academy Awards for which it was nominated, tying it with Ben-Hur and Titanic for most Academy Awards received for a film.

The trilogy appears in many “Top 10” film lists, such as Time Magazine’s All-Time 100 Movies, and in 2007 USA Today named the trilogy as the most important films of the past 25 years.

Entertainment Weekly put it on its end-of-the-decade, “best-of” list and in another TIME magazine list the trilogy ranks second in “Best Movies of the Decade”.

synopsisShort:
Screening as part of our Alfred Hitchcock Selectrospective.

From the "Master of Suspense" Alfred Hitchcock comes Dial M For Murder in a stunning 3D Restoration, providing even more thrills and chills.

Originally shot in 3D and now remastered and restored, Alfred Hitchcock's screen version of Frederick Knott's stage hit Dial M for Murder is a tasty blend of elegance and suspense casting Grace Kelly, Ray Milland and Robert Cummings as the points of a romantic triangle.

Kelly won the New York Film Critics and National Board of Review Best Actress Awards for this and two other acclaimed 1954 performances. She loves Cummings; her husband Milland plots her murder. But when he dials a Mayfair exchange to set the plot in motion, his right number gets the wrong answer - and gleaming scissors become a deadly weapon. Dial "M" for the Master of Suspense at his most stylish.

"A sophisticated, chillingly sinister thriller and one that boasts an unforgettable performance from Grace Kelly to boot." - Rotten Tomatoes

"The depth of focus, framing of characters and objects and use of the claustrophobic sets add extra pleasure to what was already a thoroughly enjoyable "perfect crime" nail-biter." - Daily Express (UK)

"The set-up is ingenious and the "kill" scene genuinely thrilling." - Guardian (UK)
title: Hitchcock Retro - Dial M for Murder in 3D

synopsisShort:

Madison Avenue advertising man Roger Thornhill finds himself thrust into the world of spies when he is mistaken for a man by the name of George Kaplan. Foreign spy Philip Vandamm and his henchman Leonard try to eliminate him but when Thornhill tries to make sense of the case, he is framed for murder. Now on the run from the police, he manages to board the 20th Century Limited bound for Chicago where he meets a beautiful blond, Eve Kendall, who helps him to evade the authorities. His world is turned upside down yet again when he learns that Eve isn't the innocent bystander he thought she was. Not all is as it seems however, leading to a dramatic rescue and escape at the top of Mt. Rushmore.

"Gripping, suspenseful, and visually iconic, this late-period Hitchcock classic laid the groundwork for countless action thrillers to follow." - Rotten Tomatoes

"The brilliant director has outdone himself by piling thrill on thrill for the delectation of an enraptured audience." - New York Daily News

"The plotting is tightly wound and the thrills are executed with devilish panache." - Times (UK)

synopsisShort:
Wild Horse Nine - Advance Screenings Fri Oct 30

From Academy Award and six-time BAFTA winning writer-director Martin McDonagh (The Banshees of Inisherin, Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri) comes WILD HORSE NINE, a blistering dark comedy about aging, guilt, friendship and the impossible attempt to negotiate with one’s own past. Spearheaded by powerhouses, Academy Award nominee John Malkovich and Academy Award winner Sam Rockwell, in two phenomenal, Oscar-worthy performances.

Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (Malkovich) and Lee (Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ (Golden Globe winner Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies and Chris begins to question whether he and Lee were ever friends, and whether there is an ulterior motive behind the trip. As Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways, Lee must grapple with the secret mission he has been tasked to complete.

"It’s top-of-game work from everyone involved, especially Malkovich as the irrepressible Chris, casually voicing the sort of things the rest of us only have nightmares about."- Toronto Star

"Wild Horse is one of the director’s most plainly enjoyable movies, thanks in no small part to the brilliant Malkovich and refreshingly sunny setting." - New York Post

"Mr. Malkovich’s wickedly entertaining, cynical yet soulful performance is the heart of a surprisingly emotional tour de force from Mr. McDonagh." - Wall Street Journal

"While Rockwell seems to do his best work with McDonagh, and this is no exception, flowers go to Malkovich who delivers arguably his finest screen performance of the 21st century." - Little White Lies

"Malkovich gives McDonagh’s pithy, tangy dialogue just the sad, soulful eccentricity that it needs to live off the page."- Variety

"Paired opposite a stellar Sam Rockwell, [Malkovich] delivers one of the great performances of his career..." - The Daily Beast
title: Wild Horse Nine - Advance Screenings

synopsisShort:
No one knows your heart like a sister.

From BAFTA nominated director Georgia Oakley (Blue Jean), comes the adaptation of Jane Austen’s beloved novel, SENSE AND SENSIBILITY, a sweeping period drama that follows three sisters’ experiences of love, loss and heartbreak.

Following the death of their father, the Dashwood sisters; the sensible and prudent Elinor, the romantic and passionate Marianne, and the young Margaret, and their mother are left financially destitute, when their family estate, Norland Park, is left to their half-brother John on the basis of a law that limits the transfer of property to male heirs. Although he is instructed to take care of his sisters, John is dissuaded of his duty by his greedy wife and they are forced to move to Barton Cottage in rural Devonshire, offered to them by a generous relative Sir John Middleton. Before leaving Norland, Elinor forms a quiet connection to Edward Ferrars, the brother of John’s wife, but they are separated when she moves and discovers his prior engagement to Lucy Steele. While Marianne struggles with her romantic aspirations when she must choose between the young and attractive John Willoughby and the older and sensible Colonel Brandon.

“The bond between the two elder Dashwoods proves the film’s real love story, a tender, tumultuous sisterhood that both actors clearly treat as the main event.” – Little White Lies

“Georgia Oakley’s adaptation of Jane Austen’s timeless, beloved 1811 novel is enchanting and beautiful, just as it should be. It’s also, in its earthy and humorous way, intensely riveting, which is also as it should be.’ – The Wrap

“Underpinning it all is the sisterly bond between Elinor and Marianne, expressed by Edgar-Jones and Creed-Miles on a level so intuitive and tender it seems almost subliminal.” – Daily Telegraph
title: Sense and Sensibility

synopsisShort:

With exclusive access to this exciting new show, Exhibition on Screen will bring these world class works to cinema audiences, with close examination of the art and leading experts exploring the immense skill and influence of this master of colour and connection. synopsisShort:
A captivating Claes Bang ('The Square') leads a superb ensemble cast in director Stéphane Demoustier’s darkly comic and thought-provoking new film, as an idealistic architect whose quest to build an ambitious landmark in Paris triggers unforeseen consequences.

1982. President François Mitterrand has launched an international competition to design the flagship project of his term: the Great Arch of La Défense, a building to match and complement the Louvre and the Arc de Triomphe. To the surprise of everyone, the commission is won by an unknown 53-year-old from Copenhagen, Otto von Spreckelsen. An outsider with only a few modernist churches to his name, the stunning submission – taking the form of a perfect white cube – becomes the talk of the capital.

Spreckelsen and his wife Liv (the marvellous Sidse Babett Knudsen) arrive in Paris to commence work, overseen by the project’s shrewd managing bureaucrat (Xavier Dolan). However, the purity of Spreckelsen’s design is quickly tested not only by budgetary constraints but the vicissitudes of politics, forcing the couple to consider whether the pursuit of perfection is worth the emotional and physical toll.

Inspired by remarkable true events, THE GREAT ARCH depicts a near-mythic story of both grand and lost illusions; a reminder that architecture, like cinema, is not just about one person's vision, but also collective perception.
title: The Great Arch

synopsisShort: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay is based on the events that gave rise to the Wall Street Journal’s shocking exposé The Facebook Files. And one chance to make amends...It’s the summer of 1983, The Witches is about to hit the shelves and Roald Dahl is making last-minute edits. Across a single afternoon at his family home, and rocked by an unexpectedly explosive confrontation, Dahl is forced to choose: make a public apology or risk his name and reputation. Inspired by real events, GIANT explores with dark humour the difference between considered opinion and dangerous rhetoric offering a complicated portrait of a fiendishly charismatic icon.

A shy lady's companion, staying in Monte Carlo with her stuffy employer, meets the wealthy Maxim de Winter. She and Max fall in love, marry and return to Manderley, his large country estate in Cornwall. Max is still troubled by the death of his first wife, Rebecca, in a boating accident the year before. The second Mrs. de Winter clashes with the housekeeper, Mrs. Danvers, and discovers that Rebecca still has a strange hold on everyone at Manderley.

"Hitchcock's first American film (and his only Best Picture winner), Rebecca is a masterpiece of haunting atmosphere, Gothic thrills, and gripping suspense." - Rotten Tomatoes

Screening as part of our Alfred Hitchcock Selectrospective.

Bruno Antony thinks he has the perfect plot to rid himself of his hated father, and when he meets tennis player Guy Haines on a train he thinks he's found the partner he needs to pull it off. His plan is relatively simple: Two strangers each agree to kill someone the other person wants gone. For example, Guy could kill his father and he could get rid of Guy's wife Miriam, freeing him to marry Anne Morton, the beautiful daughter of a U.S. Senator. Guy dismisses it all out of hand, but Bruno goes ahead with his half of the "bargain" and disposes of Miriam. When Guy balks, Bruno makes it clear that he will plant evidence to implicate Guy in her murder if he doesn't get rid of his father. Guy had also made some unfortunate statements about Miriam after she had refused to divorce him. It all leads the police to believe Guy is responsible for the murder, forcing him to deal with Bruno's mad ravings.

"A provocative premise and inventive set design lights the way for Hitchcock diabolically entertaining masterpiece." - Rotten Tomatoes

synopsisShort:
“You’re not that damned. You only like to be.”

Masuo (Kenzō KAWARASAKI), the surviving heir of the traditional Sakurada family, is trapped in a suffocating cycle of weddings and funerals, where ritual overrides meaning. Captured in Huludao, northeast China, and repatriated to Japan with his mother at the end of World War Two, Masuo experiences the reconstruction of postwar Japan through the fractures of his own family. As these ceremonies unfold with increasing absurdity, a decade-long chronicle of heartbreak, taboos and obsessive nationalism gradually emerges.

One of the most subversive works by provocative filmmaker Nagisa OSHIMA, The Ceremony delivers a scathing portrait of postwar Japan through the disintegration of the Sakurada clan. Dancing between past and present, OSHIMA’s film draws unsettling parallels between national identity and familial authority, mirroring the rise and collapse of militaristic Japan with biting irony and formal precision.

War songs, drunken chants and allusions to the American occupation underscore a society struggling to redefine itself. Both epic and deeply intimate, The Ceremony was awarded Best Film at the 1971 Kinema Junpo Awards.

“A deadly parody of one of Japan's most beloved genres, the family saga” - Dave Kehr, Chicago Reader

*Japanese with English subtitles*
title: JFF 2026 - The Ceremony on 35mm Film

synopsisShort:
Curiosity leads her where society draws the line.

Naoko ISHIKAWA (Sachiko HIDARI), the wife of a businessman, lives with her husband in a modern apartment complex overlooking a sprawling slum. Naoko’s husband, played by Eiji OKADA (Woman in the Dunes) is “an ordinary man in search of an ordinary life”. Naoko, on the other hand, finds herself yearning to find her place within a world increasingly divided by class. Their orderly, middle-class existence is disrupted when a fire in the slum draws Naoko’s attention, stirring her growing curiosity about its residents. Venturing into the area, she encounters children at play and unexpectedly encounters her husband’s former university acquaintance, now a rag dealer surviving on society’s margins. As the two become acquainted, an unlikely connection begins to form, challenging the boundaries between their vastly different worlds.

A stark and compassionate portrait of postwar Japan, She and He explores socioeconomic inequality and the quiet shame that enforces social divisions. Through gestures of everyday kindness and an unlikely bond, the film reveals an often-overlooked side of Japan's rapidly modernising society at the time. Directed by Susumu HANI, the film blends documentary realism with fiction, perfectly accompanied by a subtle, evocative score. She and He received widespread critical acclaim both in Japan and internationally after being screened at the 14th Berlin International Film Festival, where Sachiko HIDARI won the Silver Bear for Best Actress for both this film and for The Insect Woman (1963) by Shōhei IMAMURA. HIDARI also received Best Actress honors from the Blue Ribbon Awards, the Mainichi Film Awards and Kinema Junpo in 1964.

“She and He is a strangely satisfying little picture. In a rapid-fire flow of images and splintery bits and pieces of incident that level off in a singular, sure direction, Mr, Hani has drawn together a curiously compelling microcosm of a young Tokyo housewife confronting unfamiliar reality. “ - New York Times

*Japanese with English subtitles*
title: JFF 2026 - She and He on 35mm Film

synopsisShort:
Some masks come off. Some don’t.

After a devastating industrial accident leaves his face disfigured, engineer Okuyama (Tatsuya NAKADAI) withdraws from society, allowing his bandages to become both a physical and psychological barrier to ordinary life. Unable to continue a normal life as tensions mount with his wife (Machiko KYO) and colleagues, he turns to a psychiatrist (Mikijirō HIRA) who proposes an artificial mask, claiming it can “fill the gap in the mind” as much as the face.

What follows is a perilous experiment in identity. As Okuyama adopts this new face, he begins to experience a disturbing sense of liberation. Freed from the constraints of his former self, he gradually tests the limits of morality. What begins as an experiment in reinvention soon spirals into a profound identity crisis, as the mask erodes the boundary between authenticity and performance.

Directed by Hiroshi TESHIGAHARA based on the 1964 novel by Kōbō ABE and perfected by a memorable waltz theme composed by Tōru TAKEMITSU, The Face of Another is a unique and chilling meditation on jealousy and freedom, social conditioning and isolation. Combining stark modernist imagery with philosophical inquiry, TESHIGAHARA interrogates the power of anonymity, suggesting that masks do not always hide the self — in some cases, they may expose it.

“The theme is brilliantly and imaginatively explored, and the acting is potent.” - The Face of Another - Chicago Reader

“Singular and audacious” - The Face of Another: Double Vision | Current | The Criterion Collection

*Japanese with English subtitles*

synopsisShort:
“Shovelling sand to live? Or living to shovel sand?”

Amateur entomologist Junpei NIKI (Eiji OKADA) is on a three-day insect-collecting expedition in a rural coastal area, when a local villager informs him that he has missed the last bus back to town. Luckily (or perhaps, unluckily) the villager offers to find Junpei somewhere to stay for the night.

Delighted by the prospect of experiencing small-town hospitality, Junpei follows him to a woman’s house at the bottom of a vast sand pit. The woman, masterfully portrayed by Kyōko KISHIDA, welcomes him warmly into her home. It isn’t until the following morning that Junpei discovers that the wooden ladder used to access the pit has been pulled up, and he realises that his “local experience” is a far cry from the quaint encounter he had imagined.

Based on the widely translated 1962 avant-garde masterpiece novel by Kōbō ABE, Woman in the Dunes is a unique tale of entrapment and survival that has been widely regarded as a landmark of Japanese New Wave cinema. Every element of the film—from its screenplay and performances to its cinematography, direction, and haunting, minimalist score—converge to create a palpable and overwhelming sense of claustrophobia, in a seamless marriage of sound and moving image.

Shot on location at the Hamaoka sand dunes in Shizuoka Prefecture, Woman in the Dunes is a masterful visual composition, that also delves into the Sisyphean condition of the human experience. Winner of the Special Jury Prize at the 1964 Cannes Film Festival and nominated for Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film (1964) and Best Director (1965), Woman in the Dunes stands as one of the defining works of its era.

“One of the rare films able to combine realism with a parable about life.” - Roger Ebert

"Yet there is never a moment when the film doesn't look absolutely realistic, and it isn't about sand anyway, but about life.” - Roger Ebert

*Japanese with English subtitles*
title: JFF 2026 - Woman in The Dunes on 35mm Film

synopsisShort:
“I wish the sun would never rise; I love these wicked nights.”

Freshly released from prison, hardened yakuza Muraki (Ryō IKEBE) returns to Tokyo’s underworld only to discover that his gang has aligned with former rivals. Torn between the life he once knew and this new reality, Muraki seeks solace at his old gambling den, where he is taken aback by newcomer Saeko (Mariko KAGA). Beautiful and elusive, Saeko bets intensely and without remorse. Helplessly drawn to each other, the pair grow closer, pushing the limits of danger in the pursuit of ever-increasing thrills. Along the way Muraki navigates shifting gang alliances, a lingering romantic entanglement from his past and his growing fascination with Saeko’s reckless allure.


Directed by Masahiro SHINODA and based on the novel by Shintarō ISHIHARA, Pale Flower is a film noir characterised by its moody exploration of obsession and self-destruction. Interspersed with moments of humour and rich cultural references, SHINODA’s story offers a striking portrait of Japanese society at the time - a hauntingly beautiful convergence of the old and new that is known to have had a profound influence on Francis FORD COPPOLA and Martin SCORSESE. Avant-garde composer Tōru TAKEMITSU’s musical score amplifies the film’s cool, unsettling tone with unconventional sounds. Despite initial release delays in Japan due to perceived anti-social themes, Pale Flower has since garnered a strong reputation among cinephiles as one of SHINODA’s most enduring works.

"Pale Flower is one of the most haunting noirs I've seen, and something more; in 1964 it was an important work in an emerging Japanese New Wave of independent filmmakers, an exercise in existential cool." - link

*Japanese with English subtitles*
title: JFF 2026 - Pale Flower 4K Restoration

synopsisShort:
A rich tapestry of dreams colours the bleakness of hardship.

A bold departure from his famous samurai epics, Akira KUROSAWA's Dodes'ka-den is a kaleidoscopic portrait of dreamers, outcasts and survivors inhabiting a trash-strewn settlement on the outskirts of an unnamed town. At its centre is Roku-chan (Yoshitaka ZUSHI), a boy with an intellectual disability who spends his days diligently operating an imaginary streetcar, punctuating each journey with the rhythmic phrase "dodes'ka-den". Around him unfolds a tapestry of interconnected stories: a father and son envisioning a magnificent home from the shell of an abandoned car, couples trapped in cycles of conflict, neglected children and neighbours striving to preserve their dignity amid poverty. Though their circumstances are harsh, director KUROSAWA discovers humour, compassion and resilience in even the most ordinary moments.

KUROSAWA’s first colour feature saturates this bleak landscape with vivid reds, yellows and blues, creating a striking contrast between material deprivation and the boundless power of dreams. Complemented by Tōru TAKEMITSU's lyrical, bittersweet score, the narrative moves seamlessly between reality and fantasy, tragedy and transcendence. A landmark of KUROSAWA's later career, Dodes'ka-den received an Academy Award nomination for Best Foreign Language Film in 1972 and remains one of cinema's most moving celebrations of hope in the face of adversity.

“Kurosawa is one of the great humanists of cinema." - Roger Ebert

“The film remains intensely personal; its central theme of finding refuge in dreams reflects the joy Kurosawa experienced in making movies.” - Ben Sachs, Chicago Reader

*Japanese with English subtitles*
title: JFF 2026 - Dodes’ka-den on 35mm Film

synopsisShort:
Power chose their fate; they chose each other.

Set within a rigid feudal society, Samurai Rebellion follows Isaburō SASAHARA (Toshirō MIFUNE), a veteran swordsman whose son is ordered to marry Lady Ichi (Yōko TSUKASA), the disgraced former mistress of a powerful clan lord. What begins as a calculated display of authority unexpectedly blossoms into genuine love and domestic happiness. When political circumstances compel the lord to reclaim Lady Ichi, the Sasaharas refuse to surrender her, igniting an act of defiance that challenges the very foundations of the clan system.

Combining striking widescreen compositions, meticulously choreographed sword fights and Tōru TAKEMITSU's ritualistic score, Masaki KOBAYASHI crafts a gripping moral drama in which silence and sudden violence carry equal force. A stirring testament to personal freedom, human dignity and resistance to oppression, Samurai Rebellion exemplifies the director's enduring fascination with those who refuse to bow to injustice, even in the face of inevitable tragedy.

Winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the 1967 Venice Film Festival and hailed Best Film by both Kinema Junpo and the Mainichi Film Concours in 1968, this masterful jidaigeki (period drama) stands among the crowning achievements of postwar Japanese cinema.

"Amazing: stirring, subversive and, beneath their dauntingly severe surfaces, sneakily lyrical." - Other Great Artists of the Samurai Epic - The New York Times

“As extreme a samurai film as I've seen in both senses (the ethics and the violence), and one of the best. - Roger Ebert

*Japanese with English subtitles*
title: JFF 2026 - Samurai Rebellion on 35mm Film

synopsisShort:
Demons have it easier in hell.

Escaping exploitative employment with his young son, a miner (Hisashi IGAWA) searches for work, dreaming of belonging to a union. His journey leads him to a deserted mining town that had been abandoned by the male workers after the mine’s closure, leaving only a woman running an empty sweet shop (Sumie SASAKI) as the sole inhabitant. Meanwhile, the miner is shadowed by a cryptic man in an immaculate white suit (Kunie TANAKA), who photographs him from afar. Wandering in search of a better life, the miner instead finds violence and corruption waiting for him, triggering a chain of increasingly unsettling revelations.

Pitfall marked the debut feature of director Hiroshi TESHIGAHARA and the first of his landmark collaborations with novelist and playwright Kōbō ABE and composer Tōru TAKEMITSU. Through the miner’s phantom perspective, the film exposes a web of corporate manipulation and union rivalry within the machine-driven modernity of post-war Japan.

Shot in black and white by cinematographer Hiroshi SEGAWA, spoil tips and barren fields are transformed into otherworldly landscapes, creating a striking juxtaposition against archival footage of contemporary mining conditions at the time. An early milestone of the Japanese New Wave, Pitfall blends documentary techniques with fiction to create a haunting work of avant-garde surrealism.

“Impressively anomalous and consistently unpredictable, Hiroshi Teshigahara’s 1962 first feature manifests a literally fugitive quality.” - Howard Hampton for Criterion Collection

“Teshigahara's visual flair, evident in his sculptural use of wastelands and remarkable superimpositions, is matched by the singular assault of Takemitsu's unorthodox score.” - Chicago Reader

*Japanese with English subtitles*
title: JFF 2026 - Pitfall on 35mm Film

synopsisShort:
New independent documentary feature ON THE FENCE screens for one night only on Monday October 19 featuring a live Q&A with film creatives to be announced.

ON THE FENCE is a feature documentary that travels across Australia to explore one of the country’s most misunderstood and fiercely debated animals: the dingo.

Following the 5,600-kilometre Dingo Fence and the communities living on either side of it, the film brings together graziers, scientists, conservationists and First Nations voices to look at the dingo’s complicated place in Australia’s history, culture and landscape.

From livestock losses and lethal control to emerging science, ecological recovery and new approaches to coexistence, On The Fence looks at an issue that is far more complex than it first appears. Rather than reducing the story to heroes and villains, the film spends time with the people who live with these questions every day and asks what the future of dingo management in Australia could look like.

Why does the dingo inspire such strong and opposing views? What role does it still play in the Australian landscape? And after generations of conflict, is there a better way for dingoes, livestock and people to coexist?

Filmed across remote stations, conservation areas, communities and landscapes around the country, On The Fence is at times confronting, surprising and deeply Australian. It takes audiences into places and conversations rarely seen on screen, while challenging some of the assumptions we have carried about dingoes for generations.

More than a film about one animal, On The Fence is a story about land, culture, agriculture, conservation and the way Australians decide what belongs in the landscape.
title: On the Fence - Screening and Live Q&A

synopsisShort:
Special limited screenings of Everest: The Other Side from Thu Oct 29. Screening for one week only!

Elite ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson fell deeply in love while reaching the pinnacle of their sport. Their drive sharpened into a shared dream: to climb and ski the direct North Face of Everest - the most difficult and dangerous climb on the mountain and the most coveted ski line on earth. Thousands have summited the mountain via Nepal's southeast ridge, but only a handful have ever reached the top by this route and no one has successfully skied down. Already known for their extraordinary feats in the mountains and no strangers to loss, Morrison and Nelson stake everything on this daunting challenge.

“Everest: The Other Side” is directed and produced by Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin, and produced by Shannon Dill, Anna Barnes, Bob Eisenhardt, Janet Yang. The executive producers are Carolyn Bernstein, Tim Horsburgh, Nina Fialkow, David Fialkow, Andrew Reiner, Elizabeth Reiner, Moudhy Al-Rashid, Sam Frohman, Kenneth A. Howery, Jason Bowden, Will Griffith, Bettina Kadoorie. The film is edited by Bob Eisenhardt, ACE, and Simona Ferrari. The directors of photography are Clair Popkin, Jimmy Chin, Christopher Murphy.

"What seems, at first, like a thrilling but familiar daredevil documentary soon reveals a harrowing work of self-reflexive cinema that’s as tragic as it is triumphant." - The Wrap

"Beyond all the extraordinary photography of Himalayan mountain ranges, icy crevasses and plunging couloirs, Everest: The Other Side is a film about how we choose to live our lives and what it means for those we love." - Time Out

"The film’s climbing scenes are breathtakingly tense, but what sells the movie as more than mere docu-thriller is its sharp assessment of Honnold’s psychological makeup." - The Hollywood Reporter

Toast to the fools who dream on the 10th anniversary of the musical romance LA LA LAND. For one night only, enjoy the nostalgic hit featuring a live pre-show performance from The Little Bourke "Big" Band and with a sparkling wine included.

synopsisShort:
A special event screening of GEORGE MICHAEL - THE FAITH TOUR. This once lost concert film and documentary has been meticulously restored and remastered for the big screen experience.

PLUS exclusive pre-show performance from GEORGE MICHAEL RELIVED (Australia's #1 George Michael tribute show) before the film.

Tickets on sale soon!

Fri Nov 13 at 7.30pm (doors 7pm)
All tickets include a complimentary glass of sparkling wine on arrival.

Shot at the iconic Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy during the European leg of the Faith Tour in 1988, the film captures a turning point that transformed George Michael from a global superstar into a singular, era-defining artist, whose influence continues to reverberate across music, fashion, and culture today. George Michael: The Faith Tour invites audiences to experience the tour as it was meant to be seen and heard.

Directed by longtime collaborators Andy Morahan and David Austin, this once lost film has been meticulously restored and remastered, revealing George’s original vision with breathtaking clarity and power. The result is an intimate yet explosive glimpse of an artist in complete command of his voice and stagecraft.

A triumph in archival filmmaking, the film transforms footage assembled from a 14-camera shoot captured on 35mm film over two nights, into an extraordinary cinematic event.

George Michael: The Faith Tour is a celebration of ambition and fearless artistry at its peak, and a moment when the then 24-year-old George Michael changed the course of his career. This global theatrical event invites audiences to rediscover the power and joy of George Michael in full flight.



George Michael: The Faith Tour will open with an original short film by Mary McCartney, titled ‘Finding Faith’, offering an intimate introduction contextualising the tour’s cultural significance, through a sensitive and cinematic lens. In George’s own words, the film features voiceover from an unheard interview alongside unseen images captured by legendary American photographer Herb Ritts, and behind-the-scenes footage of the Faith music video.
title: George Michael - The Faith Tour Special Event

synopsisShort:
Join us for a special Q&A event preview screening of THE POLICEWOMAN with Narelle Fraser and director Claire Pasvolsky live on stage. True crime like you've never seen before!

Sun Nov 1 at 3:30pm (doors 3pm)

For nearly three decades, Victoria Police Detective Narelle Fraser confronted Australia’s darkest crimes. Her greatest weapon was empathy — but it came at a devastating cost. This is the story of how a remarkable career spiralled into a battle with trauma, and how she fought her way back to reclaim her life, her purpose, and her voice.

Australian podcast star Narelle Fraser is The Policewoman. For 27 years as a Victoria Police detective, she confronted some of the nation’s most disturbing crimes. Her unorthodox methods — grounded in deep empathy and an uncanny ability to connect — often delivered extraordinary breakthroughs, even as they raised eyebrows amongst her colleagues. But that exceptional sensitivity also left her vulnerable. After decades on the frontline, Narelle was overwhelmed by cumulative trauma and PTSD, fighting to hold onto her identity as the job threatened to consume her.

This immersive true crime documentary traces Narelle’s journey through meticulously crafted miniature dioramas — a world she controls, reshapes, and revisits to map her descent and recovery. It’s an extraordinary story of confronting the darkest corners of human nature, battling the psychological toll of service, and clawing back triumph from the edge.

A special 30th Anniversary screening of Peter Jackson's criminally underrated cult classic The Frighteners, starring Michael J. Fox in his last major feature film role.

Once an architect, Frank Bannister (Michael J. Fox) now passes himself off as an exorcist of evil spirits. To bolster his facade, he claims his "special" gift is the result of a car accident that killed his wife. But what he does not count on is more people dying in the small town where he lives. Based on a story by O'Bannon and Ronald Shusett, it follows the crew of the commercial space tug Nostromo, who, after coming across a mysterious derelict spaceship on an undiscovered moon, find themselves up against an aggressive and deadly extra-terrestrial set loose on the Nostromo.

Meek flower shop assistant Seymour (Rick Moranis) pines for co-worker Audrey (Ellen Greene). During a total eclipse, he discovers an unusual plant he names Audrey II, which feeds only on human flesh and blood. The growing plant attracts a great deal of business for the previously struggling store. After Seymour feeds Audrey's boyfriend, Orin (Steve Martin), to the plant after Orin's accidental death, he must come up with more bodies for the increasingly bloodthirsty plant.

"Remixing Roger Corman's B-movie by way of the Off-Broadway musical, Little Shop of Horrors offers camp, horror and catchy tunes in equal measure -- plus some inspired cameos by the likes of Steve Martin and Bill Murray." - Rotten Tomatoes
title: Little Shop of Horrors - 40th Anniversary

synopsisShort:
A special 35th Anniversary screening of psychological horror THE SILENCE OF THE LAMBS, starring Jodie Foster and Anthony Hopkins in his signature role as iconic villain Hannibal Lectre. Screening in 4K Restoration.

Young FBI agent Clarice Starling is assigned to help find a missing woman to save her from a psychopathic serial killer who skins his victims. Clarice attempts to gain a better insight into the twisted mind of the killer by talking to another psychopath: Hannibal Lecter, who used to be a respected psychiatrist. FBI agent Jack Crawford believes that Lecter, who is also a very powerful and clever mind manipulator, has the answers to their questions and can help locate the killer. However, Clarice must first gain Lecter's confidence before the inmate will give away any information.

"Director Jonathan Demme's smart, taut thriller teeters on the edge between psychological study and all-out horror, and benefits greatly from stellar performances by Anthony Hopkins and Jodie Foster." - Rotten Tomatoes

Bonnie (Neve Campbell), Rochelle (Rachel True) and Nancy (Fairuza Balk), like Sarah herself, all have troubled backgrounds, which combined with their nascent powers lead to dangerous consequences. When a minor spell causes a fellow student to lose her hair, the girls grow power-mad.

"It's Teen Witch for the Nineties: dark, brooding, dangerous, and, come to think of it, a lot like high school." - Austin Chronicle

A special Halloween season screening of THE EXORCIST, screening in a 4K Restoration of the Director's Cut.

Winner of 1973 Oscars for Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Sound Mixing, The Exorcist remains one of the most shocking and gripping movies in the history of cinema and is a regular feature on lists of the scariest movies ever made.

When young Regan (Linda Blair) starts acting odd -- levitating, speaking in tongues -- her worried mother (Ellen Burstyn) seeks medical help, only to hit a dead end. A local priest (Jason Miller), however, thinks the girl may be seized by the devil. The priest makes a request to perform an exorcism, and the church sends in an expert (Max von Sydow) to help with the difficult job.

"The Exorcist rides its supernatural theme to magical effect, with remarkable special effects and an eerie atmosphere, resulting in one of the scariest films of all time." - Rotten Tomatoes
title: The Exorcist - Directors Cut 4K Restoration

synopsisShort:
A special Northside Exclusive limited season of acclaimed new film TENZING starring Tom Hiddleston and Genden Phuntsok as Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, the first climbers to ever summit Mount Everest.

Based on true events, “Tenzing” chronicles the little-known story of Tenzing Norgay, a gifted Himalayan climber who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary, was the first to summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa, Tenzing finds an ally in expedition secretary Jill Henderson. Together, they persuade Colonel John Hunt that Tenzing belongs on the British climbing team, rather than merely serving it. Where Western climbers see “Everest” as something to be conquered, Tenzing reveres “Chomolungma” as the sacred mother goddess. What follows is an ascent defined as much by the tensions between backgrounds, classes and competing ambitions as by the perils of the mountain itself. But high above the world, empire, rank and aspiration fall away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — and for Tenzing, the fulfillment of both a lifelong dream and a spiritual calling.

"Guided by Genden Phuntsok’s powerful performance and supported by Tom Hiddleston, Willem Dafoe, Caitríona Balfe, and Thinley Lhamo, the film is an inspirational biographical epic elevated by an extraordinary life and crowd-pleasing filmmaking." - Next Best Picture

"At its best, Tenzing is a personal story and a fascinating exploration of the varied local culture’s relationship to the as-of-yet untamed deity." - Awards Watch

In post–civil war Spain, 10-year-old Ofelia moves with her pregnant mother to live under the control of her cruel stepfather. To return to her true father, she must complete a series of surreal and perilous tasks that blur the line between reality and fantasy.

synopsisShort:
OZZY & BLACK SABBATH: BACK TO THE BEGINNING - Two shows only! A must see for fans.

OZZY & BLACK SABBATH: BACK TO THE BEGINNING documents a landmark moment in music history: Ozzy Osbourne’s historic final farewell performance for his fans at Villa Park stadium in his Birmingham hometown--captured just 17 days before his untimely passing. This is an historic and intimate farewell to Ozzy and the band that changed music forever.

The Federation calls on Adm. James T. Kirk (William Shatner) and the crew of the Starship Enterprise to contain an immense nimbused object that's on a crash course with Earth. After investigating, the crew discovers that the alien cloud harbors artificial intelligence with an ominous primary directive. Crisis strikes when a probe dispatched by the energy cloud attacks the crew, abducting navigator Lt. Ilia (Persis Khambatta). An android look-alike containing her memories shows up soon after.

It is the 23rd century. Admiral James T. Kirk is an instructor at Starfleet Academy and feeling old; the prospect of attending his ship, the USS Enterprise--now a training ship--on a two-week cadet cruise does not make him feel any younger. But the training cruise becomes a deadly serious mission when his nemesis Khan Noonien Singh--infamous conqueror from late 20th century Earth--appears after years of exile. Khan later revealed that the planet Ceti Alpha VI exploded, and shifted the orbit of the fifth planet as a Mars-like haven. He begins capturing Project Genesis, a top secret device holding the power of creation itself, and schemes the utter destruction of Kirk.

synopsisShort:
AN EVENING WITH JELENA DOKIC LIVE ON STAGE TO TALK ABOUT HER NEW BOOK.

Stop surviving, start living free.
Join us for AN EVENING WITH JELENA DOKIC as the former world No. 4 tennis player, bestselling author, two-time Logie Award winner, commentator, presenter and motivational speaker launches her brand-new book 'Live Free' on November 17.

In 'Live Free', Jelena Dokic shares the insights and tools that helped her reclaim her voice and her life - and shows you how you might be able to do the same. 'My mission is to clear the path ahead just a little, so that you won't have to endure it alone. I want you to be free to live the life you deserve.'

No matter where this book finds you – on your darkest day or in the messy midst of healing – know that you are not alone. If you feel stuck, lost, overwhelmed or held back by your past and your life, there can be a way forward. Jelena’s approach is built on four essential pillars:

• Finding self-worth
• Vulnerability as a superpower
• Shattering the myth of perfection
• Finding peace and healing

Grounded in lived experience, she draws on her journey through hardship in her early life, adversity in her tennis career and the abuse she suffered at the hands of her father, which led to trauma and mental health challenges.

She also reflects on dealing with doubters and shaming. Through honest guidance, personal lessons, and practical tools and exercises, Live Free helps you to break old patterns and move forward with confidence. To lead with self-belief. To find strength in vulnerability.

To let go of perfection and build a sense of self-worth so you can live free from shame.

BOOKS WILL BE AVAILABLE FOR SALE AND JELENA DOKIC WILL BE SIGNING COPIES.

About Leah Berry:
Jazz Vocalist Leah Berry is quickly establishing herself as a notable emerging figure in the Sydney jazz scene. She is an impressive performer, improviser and lyricist, who captivates audiences with her storytelling, and velvety tone. Leah concluded her bachelor’s degree studying Jazz Vocal Performance at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music in 2024 and is eager to continue her growth as a musician in Sydney and Australia.
In October 2025, the Leah Berry Quartet performed at the SIMA International Women’s Jazz Festival, spotlighting the sounds of Betty Carter through her own voice.
Leah has performed with Australian jazz legend James Morrison, and as part of the Inner West Jazz Fest in August 2025, Leah joined forces with jazz veteran Mike Nock, presenting a set of her lyrics to his compositions, solidifying her unique voice in the Australian jazz scene as a lyricist and musician. Leah and Mike have since recorded a remarkable album of their music entitled ‘The Gift’, with the incomparable Jonathan Zwartz on double bass and Laurence Pike on drums.
Leah has also recently recorded an album of some of her favourite standards with her own quartet, to be released early 2027.
